title: According to the effort (Avot 5:23)
hookLine: Ben Hei Hei: the reward is according to the effort
tomorrow: if the answer is no, why keep doing the thing at all?

cards: Opening night is done. The bows, the flowers from the lobby, the photos. Then the quiet in the car on the way home, and a question that sneaks in once the applause stops.
What if nobody who mattered was watching? Was the work worth it either way? Ben Hei Hei answers in a single short line of Aramaic.

teach.b: Ben Hei Hei says: lefum tza'ara agra. According to the effort is the reward. The word tza'ara is effort, and it can also mean pain: what it cost you.
Notice what the line leaves out. It doesn't say according to the result. It doesn't say according to who saw.
The reward follows the cost, not the scoreboard.
That's the life part, for a week like this one: a test you studied for and still did badly on, a job you gave everything and didn't get, a show that went well with no one important in the seats.
Ben Hei Hei measures the thing you actually control. And the Talmud gives his name a second scene.

There, Bar Hei Hei asks Hillel a question, and Hillel answers that a student who reviews a lesson a hundred times can't be compared to one who reviews it a hundred and one. The extra time is the one that costs.
That fits right after yesterday's turn it and turn it. One more turn, when you're tired of turning, is where the reward lives.
None of this says results don't matter.
It says they aren't the measure.

how: Ben Hei Hei's Aramaic line, lefum tza'ara agra, is quoted in Jewish learning as a word of encouragement for hard study or hard work; it is read with chapter five of Avot on summer Shabbat afternoons.

games.q: what does “according to the effort” mean?
o: the reward goes to whoever finishes first
the reward follows how hard you tried
a prize paid once the work is judged

games.q: according to the effort — tap the pairs.
p: according to the effort, the reward

s: Ben Hei Hei says the reward matches the result
according to the effort, what it cost, is the reward.
his line is in Aramaic, not Hebrew
lefum tza'ara agra: according to the effort, the reward.
in the Talmud, Hillel tells Bar Hei Hei that reviewing 101 times beats 100
the extra time is the one that costs.

games.q: two coworkers finish the same project. one coasted on talent; one fought for every step. by Ben Hei Hei's measure, whose reward is greater?
o: the one who struggled: the reward follows the effort, not the result.
the same for both: the project got done, so it counts the same.
the talented one: an easy result shows the greater skill.
games.why: lefum tza'ara agra: according to the effort is the reward. the result is the same; the cost is not.

practice: Pick one small thing within reach: fold a shirt, straighten a shelf, write your name. Do it now, slowly, with full effort, as if it were the only task of the day.
When it's done, rest your hands and notice what the care itself was like.

wordCard.voice: According to the effort: Ben Hei Hei's measure for the reward. What it cost, not what it won.

orig.note: Aramaic: according to the effort, the reward (Avot 5:23).

carryVoice: Carry it out the door: according to the effort, not the applause, not the phone call. Good night.

sources.ref: Babylonian Talmud, Chagigah 9b (Bar Hei Hei and Hillel)
